crossrefs.text: He who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from distress.
Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
A foolʼs mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
We all stumble in many ways. If anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.
My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.
I said, “I will watch my ways so that I will not sin with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle as long as the wicked are present.”
When words are many, sin is unavoidable, but he who restrains his lips is wise.
He who reveals secrets is a constant gossip; avoid the one who babbles with his lips.
An inheritance gained quickly will not be blessed in the end.
Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.
The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until midday.
He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.
One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.
For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like other men—swindlers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.
He shall certainly be cut off, because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment; his guilt remains on him.”
She is a tree of life to those who embrace her, and those who lay hold of her are blessed.
But they mocked the messengers of God, despising His words and scoffing at His prophets, until the wrath of the LORD against His people was stirred up beyond remedy.
As for me, I will behold Your face in righteousness; when I awake, I will be satisfied in Your presence.
My soul faints for Your salvation; I wait for Your word.
Though I am like a wineskin dried up by smoke, I do not forget Your statutes.
Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but that you may be fully rewarded.
Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning; for some of you are ignorant of God. I say this to your shame.

To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
He who listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.
Leave your folly behind, and you will live; walk in the way of understanding.”
Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
And: “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”
